author.social.lead: His focus goes beyond today's problems to Kazakhstan's future in the decades ahead.

issues.text: The return of kandases (ethnic Kazakh returnees) to their historical homeland
Adapting to a new environment and finding a place in society

author.social.body:
For Omar Bekmurat, every family that returns home adds to Kazakhstan's demographic potential, and every child is a future citizen of the country. That is why he cares deeply about the difficulties kandases face when preparing documents, obtaining a residence permit and citizenship, accessing education, finding a job and starting a business.

He does not stop at solving individual cases; he looks at why these difficulties arise. He studies people's appeals and life situations, sends official proposals to government agencies and puts forward initiatives to make migration procedures clearer and more accessible.

Behind every piece of this work lies one person's fate, one family's hope and the future of someone who wants to return to their historical homeland.

author.stage.title: National art — a legacy entrusted to future generations
author.stage.lead: As a director-choreographer, he sees national dance as more than a stage performance. Kazakh dance is a treasure that carries the character, history, worldview and spirit of the people.
author.stage.studioText: It teaches children and teenagers not only dance moves, but also stage culture, discipline, responsibility and respect for national art.
author.stage.groupsNote: Blending tradition and innovation, they show what Kazakh dance can do on the modern stage.
author.stage.projectsNote: National identity grows into a movement shared by many, and art keeps the bond between generations alive.

author.business.title: Connecting people and opportunities
author.business.lead: Speaking Kazakh, Chinese and Russian has helped him understand in depth the problems of people from very different backgrounds. Language is more than a means of communication: it is a bridge that connects the individual and society, the citizen and the state, and the cultures and business communities of two countries.
author.business.cardText: A trusted bridge between Kazakhstan and China — an international translation and document support center in Astana.
author.business.cardNote: The ultimate goal of every service is to save people time, help them find the right path through complex procedures and give them the chance to start a new life.

author.goals.title: The common thread of his initiatives
author.goals.lead: For him, serving the country does not begin with grand words. It begins with paying attention to one person's problem, passing national art on to one child and helping one family put down roots in their historical homeland.

items.q: Which documents should I prepare before leaving China?
items.a: Usually you'll need your passport, birth certificate, marriage certificate and education documents. We'll tell you in advance which documents need notarization and an apostille — it's much easier to get these done in China before you leave.

items.q: My name is written differently in Chinese across my documents. What should I do?
items.a: This happens a lot. When translating, we make sure your name is spelled the same way in every document, and we also cross-check dates, addresses, seals and stamps.

items.q: How much do your services cost?

items.q: Do you issue the "Ata Zholy" card or grant citizenship?
items.a: No. The final decision is made by the competent government authorities of the Republic of Kazakhstan. We help you prepare your documents correctly, completely and in line with the requirements.

items.q: Do you also work with companies?

seo.kaztest.description: A free practice test in the KAZTEST format: listening and reading, 60 questions, 70 minutes, with answers. Prepare for a permanent residence permit or kandas status.

kaztest.head.title: KAZTEST practice test
kaztest.head.lead: Practice in the official exam format: Listening (Тыңдалым) first, then Reading (Оқылым), against the clock. At the end, you'll see right away which questions you answered correctly and which you got wrong.
kaztest.head.ctaNote: Your answers are saved only on your own device.

kaztest.law.title: Kazakh language testing for permanent residence and kandas status
kaztest.law.text: A pilot project has been running since February 13, 2026: when a foreign national is granted a permanent residence permit, or when kandas (ethnic Kazakh returnee) status is granted or extended, knowledge of the state language is tested through the online KAZTEST — at least level A1 (beginner) is required. To pass, you need to score at least 70% in each section. The pilot project runs until December 31, 2026.
kaztest.law.sources: Source: the pilot project document, Adilet · Official testing: National Testing Center

kaztest.list.title: Choose a test
kaztest.list.aside: Each test follows the structure of the official exam. New tests are added regularly.
kaztest.list.note: The test is in Cyrillic script, just like the official exam. The tests were written by BASTAU LINE in the official exam format; they are not materials of the National Testing Center.

kaztest.how.title: In the same order as the official exam
kaztest.how.aside: All you need is an internet connection and headphones. You can pause the test at any time and continue later.

steps.title: Choose a test
steps.text: Pick a test and press "Start the test" — the timer starts running.

steps.title: Listening (Тыңдалым)
steps.text: Listen to the recordings and answer the questions on each dialogue and text.

steps.title: Reading (Оқылым)
steps.text: The passage appears next to the question — read it and choose the correct answer.

steps.title: Results
steps.text: You'll see right away whether you reached the 70% pass mark in each section. You can review your mistakes and retake the test.

kaztest.faq.title: About KAZTEST
kaztest.faq.lead: Not sure which requirement applies to you? Write to us.

items.a: It's the national system for assessing proficiency in the Kazakh language. The test is run by the National Testing Center, and a certificate is issued based on the results.

Under the 2026 pilot project, it applies to foreign nationals applying for a permanent residence permit in Kazakhstan and to applicants for kandas status or its extension. The minimum required level is A1.

There is a separate test for citizenship: the state language, the basics of the Constitution and the history of Kazakhstan. Kandases are exempt from this test (Zakon.kz, 19.01.2026).

items.q: Is the practice test similar to the official exam?
items.a: Yes: 60 questions — 20 in Listening (Тыңдалым) and 40 in Reading (Оқылым) — and 70 minutes in total. To pass, you need at least 70% correct answers in each section: 14 in Listening and 28 in Reading. The results show "passed" or "failed" for each section.

items.q: Where do I register for the official test?
items.a: On the National Testing Center website: testcenter.kz. We'll help you plan which test to take and when, together with your documents.

items.q: Are these questions taken from the official exam?
items.a: No. BASTAU LINE wrote these tests itself, following the structure and level of the official exam: the sections, number of questions, time and task types are the same, while the texts, dialogues and questions are new. Your result shows how well prepared you are, but it does not guarantee your result in the official exam.

kaztest.cross.text: A Kazakh language course plus document preparation for kandas status and a permanent residence permit — all at BASTAU LINE.

faq.q: Do I have to give up my Chinese citizenship?
faq.a: No. The main feature of the "Ata Zholy" card is that you keep your foreign citizenship.

faq.q: Can my family get the card too?
faq.a: Yes, your family members can live in Kazakhstan with you. We'll help prepare their documents too.
No. The final decision is made by the competent government authorities of the Republic of Kazakhstan. We help make sure your documents are correct, complete and meet the requirements.

faq.q: Can I get citizenship later if I have the card?
faq.a: Yes, if you wish. But cardholders are not required to take up citizenship.

faq.q: How is it different from kandas status?
faq.a:
Kandas status is for those who move for good and later become citizens; it is granted for 1 year. The "Ata Zholy" card is for those who want to keep their citizenship while living and working in Kazakhstan long-term.

apostille.title: Apostille for Chinese documents: a step-by-step guide
apostille.excerpt: From the notary office to the foreign affairs office — what to do, where, and in what order.
apostille.bodyHtml:
In the past, to use a document issued in China in Kazakhstan, you had to go through lengthy consular legalization: first China's foreign affairs authorities certified it, then Kazakhstan's embassy or consulate in China. This could take months and required a separate fee for each document.

What has changed?

Since November 7, 2023, the People's Republic of China has been a party to the 1961 Hague Convention abolishing the requirement to legalize foreign public documents (the Apostille Convention). Kazakhstan joined this convention long ago. This means that a Chinese document now needs just one apostille to be valid in Kazakhstan as well.

In shortNo more consular legalization. In China: notarization + apostille. In Kazakhstan: translation and notarization of the translation.

Which documents need an apostille?

  • Birth certificate — for kandas (ethnic Kazakh returnee) status and citizenship
  • Marriage certificate and children's birth certificates
  • Diploma and its supplement — for admission to study and diploma recognition
  • Certificate of no criminal record — for the "Ata Zholy" ("Ancestral Path") card and a residence permit
  • A document confirming your ethnicity, if it isn't shown on your ID

Steps

  1. Notary office. Get the document notarized at the notary office (公证处) in your hometown. In most cases, the notarial certificate comes with an English translation.
  2. Apostille. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC or its authorized local foreign affairs office puts an apostille on the notarial certificate.
  3. Translation. Once you arrive in Kazakhstan, we translate the document together with its apostille into Kazakh or Russian.
  4. Certifying the translation. A notary certifies the translator's signature — your document is now ready to be submitted via enbek.kz, to the migration service or to a university.

Common mistakes

The most common mistake is starting to gather documents only after arriving in Kazakhstan. Then everything has to be done through relatives in China with a power of attorney, which makes the process two to three times longer. The second mistake is having your name spelled differently in different documents: the Latin spelling in your passport, the Chinese characters on your certificates and the Cyrillic spelling in the translation must all match.

TipSettle the Cyrillic spelling of your name in your very first translation, and use exactly the same spelling in every document after that.

sharyn.name: Charyn Canyon
sharyn.lead: One of the most beautiful places in Kazakhstan — locals call it the "valley of fortified castles."
sharyn.bodyHtml:
Charyn Canyon lies 195 km from the city of Almaty. It is 200 km long, and its rock formations rise from 150 to 300 meters. The "Valley of Towers," which is especially popular with tourists, is 2 km long and 20–80 m wide.

Charyn is often compared to America's Grand Canyon and called its little brother. Huge rocks that seem to touch the sky resemble a fairy-tale city that built itself: their shapes look strikingly like man-made buildings and towers.

Images of wild animals show that birds and animals lived in this area as far back as the Paleolithic. Barberry and turanga poplar grow in the lower part of the canyon.

kolsai.name: Kolsai Lakes
kolsai.lead: A chain of three lakes in the Northern Tien Shan: Lower, Middle and Upper Kolsai.
kolsai.bodyHtml:
The Kolsai Lakes are a system of three lakes in the Northern Tien Shan, which links the Kungei Alatau and Trans-Ili Alatau ranges. They lie one after another at different altitudes along the Kolsai River.

Upper Kolsai lies 2,650 m above sea level, Middle Kolsai at 2,280 m and Lower Kolsai at 1,800 m. The lower lake is 1,520 m long and 222 m wide on average.

The neighboring Lake Kaindy was formed by a powerful earthquake in 1911: water flooded the valley, and the trees ended up underwater. Because the lake water stays at around +6°C even in summer, the needles on the trees have survived to this day.

khantengri.name: Khan Tengri
khantengri.lead: The most beautiful peak of the Tien Shan, which Kazakhs call "Aspantau" — it stands where the borders of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and China meet.
khantengri.bodyHtml:
Khan Tengri is one of the high peaks of the Tien Shan, which Kazakhs call "Aspantau." Its southeastern side belongs to Kazakhstan, its eastern side to China and its western side to Kyrgyzstan.

Rising to more than 7,000 meters, it is counted among the most beautiful peaks in the world. Until 1960, local people called it Khantengir.

The marble walls of this sharp, four-sided pyramid catch the eye from far away. Climbers reach the summit via the South and North Inylchek glaciers.

muztau.name: Belukha
muztau.fact: Highest peak of the Altai · 4,506 m
muztau.lead: The highest glacier-capped peak of the Altai Mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan. Kazakhs called it Aksumbi and Aktaiky.
muztau.bodyHtml:
Belukha (Muztau in Kazakh) is the highest glacier-capped peak of the Altai Mountains in Russia and Kazakhstan (4,506 m). It rises on the eastern side of the Katun Range, near the border between Kazakhstan and the Altai region.

Near its summit lie the Greater and Lesser Berel and Mensu glaciers, which give rise to the Katun River. The river basins connected with Belukha contain 162 glaciers covering 146 square kilometers.

The people of Altai affectionately call Belukha "the abode of God" and "the Great Elder." Perhaps it got these names because it is covered in eternal snow from top to bottom.

alakol.name: Lake Alakol
alakol.lead: A closed lake rich in iodine and salts, known for its healing properties. Silk Road caravans once passed along its shores.
alakol.bodyHtml:
Alakol is a closed lake with no outflow, located in Almaty and East Kazakhstan regions. More than 15 rivers flow into it.

Its water is rich in minerals, iodine and salt, and its health benefits have been medically proven. Travelers on the Silk Road are said to have rested on its shores and drawn strength from its waters.

Between the 12th and 19th centuries, the lake was known by several names: Turge-Nor, Alaktagol and Alateniz.

okzhetpes.name: Okzhetpes
okzhetpes.lead: A granite rock rising above the clear waters of Lake Auliekol. Shokan Ualikhanov collected more than 15 legends about it.
okzhetpes.bodyHtml:
Okzhetpes stands next to Mount Kokshe, the highest point of the Kokshetau Upland. It is made of granite, with steep slopes where pine and birch grow.

Many legends are told about this rock above the clear waters of Lake Auliekol. Shokan Ualikhanov collected more than 15 legends and tales, and Saken Seifullin told the story of Okzhetpes in his poem "Kokshetau."

korgalzhyn.name: Korgalzhyn Nature Reserve
korgalzhyn.lead: Around 60 lakes that are home to millions of birds. Three of the world's 8 bird migration routes pass through Lake Tengiz.
korgalzhyn.bodyHtml:
Korgalzhyn Nature Reserve lies 120 km southwest of the city of Astana. In 1968, it was re-established as a nature reserve by government decree. It covers 258,963 hectares.

There are 8 bird migration routes in the world, and three of them cross Lake Tengiz in this reserve. That is why millions of birds live on Korgalzhyn's nearly 70 lakes.

The reserve belongs to Group "A" under the Ramsar Convention, and in 2007 its lakes were designated an Important Bird Area (IBA) of international significance.

tanbaly.name: Tamgaly Petroglyphs
tanbaly.lead: One of the oldest monuments of Zhetysu — thousands of images carved into the rock since the Bronze Age.
tanbaly.bodyHtml:
This archaeological complex lies in the southeastern part of the Chu-Ili Mountains in Almaty Region, 170 km northwest of Almaty.

The Tamgaly complex includes more than 5,000 petroglyphs from different historical periods, as well as settlements, burial grounds and sacrificial sites. Its most valuable part is the petroglyphs of the Middle Bronze Age.

Researchers particularly highlight the high aesthetic value and spiritual impact of the Tamgaly petroglyphs.

yassawi.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
yassawi.lead: A jewel of medieval architecture in Turkistan and the spiritual center of the Turkic world.
yassawi.bodyHtml:
The Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi is a jewel of medieval architecture in Turkistan. It was built at the end of the 14th century by order of Amir Timur over the grave of the great thinker Khoja Ahmed Yasawi.

In 2003, the mausoleum was added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. For centuries, this towering building with its blue dome has been a sacred place of pilgrimage for the peoples of Central Asia.

otyrar.name: Ancient city of Otrar
otyrar.lead: A major center of trade and learning on the Silk Road, and the capital of the region where the great thinker al-Farabi was born.
otyrar.bodyHtml:
The ancient city of Otrar lies 7 km northwest of Shauildir, the center of Otrar District. In history it is also known as Turarband, Tarband and Farab.

The city was an important center on the trade route linking Iran and Central Asia with Siberia, Mongolia and China. Otrar was the capital of the region where Abu Nasr al-Farabi was born.

beket.name: Beket Ata Mosque
beket.lead: The most sacred pilgrimage site in Mangystau — an underground mosque carved into the rock by Beket Ata.
beket.bodyHtml:
Beket Myrzagululy (1750–1813) was a prominent Kazakh religious figure, educator and warrior. A master builder, he carved underground mosques in the Mangystau, Atyrau and Ustyurt areas, where children were taught.

In the underground mosque at Ogylandy, he founded a Sufi school. Today the place is known as a sacred site that gives people spiritual nourishment and shows the way to those who have lost it.

ulytau.name: Ulytau
ulytau.fact: The heart of the Kazakh land
ulytau.lead: The highest point of western Saryarka. A land where khans were raised on white felt, and which Asan Kaigy called Zheruiyk (the promised land).
ulytau.bodyHtml:
Ulytau covers the southeast of the Turgai Trough and the northern part of Betpak-Dala. It is not only the highest point of western Saryarka, but also its "heart" and the "center of the world."

It was here that the Kazakhs raised their sultans on white felt and proclaimed them khans. Jochi Khan, Alasha Khan and Tokhtamysh Khan, as well as the warrior Edige, are buried here. Asan Kaigy called this land Zheruiyk, a promised land where the Kazakh people could live well.

zhidebai.name: Zhidebai-Borili
zhidebai.lead: A historical and cultural complex that gives a full picture of Abai's life and work.
zhidebai.bodyHtml:
The complex is located in the settlement of Zhidebai in Abai District. Abai's winter home, inherited from Kunanbai in 1884, was turned into a house museum.

The items in the museum's five rooms and three halls were collected from the poet's relatives, friends and contemporaries. The outside of the house still looks as it did in Abai's time.

baiterek.name: Baiterek
baiterek.lead: A symbol of the independent country: its height of 97 meters stands for 1997, when the capital moved to Astana.
baiterek.bodyHtml:
The Baiterek monument in the center of Astana is a symbol of the independent Kazakh state and of its people's revival and renewal. The structure rises to 97 meters, a reference to 1997, the year the new capital was proclaimed.

The main idea behind the monument is the World Tree. The "Bata" (Blessing) composition at the top holds the blessings of the leaders of world religions who gathered in Astana in 2003.

berel.name: Berel Kurgans
berel.fact: More than 70 burial mounds · Saka period
berel.lead: A famous Saka and Turkic burial ground where permafrost has kept clothing, horse gear and wooden objects from decaying.
berel.bodyHtml:
The Berel burial ground lies 7–8 km southwest of the village of Berel in Katon-Karagay District. The earliest mounds date back to the 4th–3rd centuries BC, and the later ones to the ancient Turkic period.

Thanks to the permafrost inside the large mounds, clothing, horse harnesses, wooden objects and items made of leather and felt have been well preserved. The site was studied by V. Radlov in 1865, and Z. Samashev has been researching it since 1998.

bayanaul.name: Konyr Aulie Cave
bayanaul.lead: A sacred place where people have come to make wishes since ancient times. Mashhur Zhusup called it "the place where saints ask Allah for His decree."
bayanaul.bodyHtml:
This sacred cave in the Bayanaul Mountains lies three kilometers from Lake Zhasybay. Known as Konyr Aulie or the Aulie Tas cave, it has long been regarded as the blessed heart of Bayanaul.

Water constantly collects in a cauldron-like hollow deep inside the cave; it is considered sacred and healing for the sick. Mashhur Zhusup praised the sanctity of this place and called it "the place where saints ask Allah for His decree."

tamshybulak.name: Tamshybulak
tamshybulak.lead: A healing spring that breaks through stone walls and flows drop by drop. Shokan Ualikhanov studied it in 1859–1865.
tamshybulak.bodyHtml:
Tamshybulak is in the center of the village of Kapal in Aksu District. Breaking through ancient stone walls and gathering drop by drop, the spring does not freeze even in winter.

Since ancient times, local people have used its water to treat various illnesses. The first written records of Tamshybulak were made by Shokan Ualikhanov.

esik.name: Esik Kurgans
esik.lead: A burial ground of Saka kings where the "Golden Man," one of the symbols of independent Kazakhstan, was found in 1969.
esik.bodyHtml:
The Esik Kurgans are a burial ground of Saka kings at the foot of the Trans-Ili Alatau. In 1969, the remains of a warrior in golden clothing — the famous "Golden Man" — were found in one of the mounds here.

Today the "Golden Man" stands atop Kazakhstan's Independence Monument, and an open-air museum operates near the kurgans.
